title: Why Kunti walked away
hookLine: her sons finally rule, and Kunti walks into the forest: the Hindu stage of life for letting go
carry: vanaprastha: a season for letting go
tomorrow: The blessing that names no side
last: YOUR OWN DHARMA IS FACED, NOT AVOIDED.

cards: A small procession leaves Hastinapura through the gate. In it walks an old blind king, Dhritarashtra, whose sons died in the war. His hand rests on the shoulder of his wife, Gandhari, her eyes bound with cloth.
And Gandhari's hand rests on the shoulder of the woman leading them both: Kunti. The Pandavas are on the throne at last.

Their mother has everything the war was fought for, and she is walking away from it, into the forest, guiding the parents of the men her sons killed. Her sons run after her. Today: Kunti's last word to them.

teach.b: The scene is in the Mahabharata's Book of the Hermitage. Dhritarashtra has decided to end his days in the forest, and Gandhari goes with him. Kunti's sons assume their mother will stay.
She doesn't. Bhima puts the hard question into words, in paraphrase: you roused us to fight, and now that the kingdom is ours, you leave it?
Kunti's answer is the center of the scene. I urged you on so that you wouldn't live in humiliation, so that Draupadi would not be wronged again. Not so that I could enjoy a kingdom.
I had my time as a queen, with your father. Now I will serve my elders in the forest. Go back.
Hindu law books describe life in four stages, the ashramas: student, householder, then vanaprastha, the forest-dweller, and last the renouncer.

teach.h: VANAPRASTHA: A TIME TO LET GO
teach.b: The Laws of Manu put it simply: when a householder sees wrinkles, gray hair and his children's children, it is time for the forest.
Vanaprastha means stepping back from running the house and the money and the fights, and turning the rest of life toward God.
Kunti fought hard in her householder's season, for duty, not the prize, so when the season turns, there's nothing she needs to hold. Few Hindus walk into a real forest now.

But you'll see the stage in plenty of families: a grandparent who hands over the kitchen and the keys and spends the mornings at the temple or on pilgrimage. Many teachers read that as vanaprastha, kept the modern way.

how: The four stages of life, the ashramas, are set out in Hindu law books such as the Laws of Manu; few people now leave for a real forest, but many Hindu grandparents step back from running the household and give their days to prayer, temple and pilgrimage, which many teachers describe as vanaprastha today.

o: a queen who rules on after her sons win the war
a mother who stays in the palace to care for Gandhari
the mother who leaves the throne her sons won for the forest stage of life

games.q: the four stages of life — tap the pairs.
p: leaves the kingdom for the forest

s: Kunti stays in the palace to enjoy her sons' reign
she walks into the forest with Dhritarashtra and Gandhari.
Kunti says she urged the war for her own enjoyment of the kingdom
she urged them on for their honor and Draupadi's, not to enjoy a kingdom herself.
vanaprastha is the stage of life for stepping back from the household and turning toward God
the law books name it third of four: student, householder, forest-dweller, renouncer.

games.q: you're Kunti. your sons rule at last, and the blind king and Gandhari are leaving for the forest. what do you do?
o: stay and enjoy the kingdom you fought for.
go with them: your householder season is over.
send servants to look after them.
games.why: she leaves with them. she had her time as queen; she fought for duty, not the prize, so she can let it go. that's vanaprastha.

practice: Rest one hand lightly on your own shoulder, the way Gandhari's rested on Kunti's, and bring to mind one thing you're holding tightly in this season of your life: a role, a say in things, a plan.

Ask gently whether it's yours to keep, or one day yours to hand on. Stay with that for a few breaths without deciding anything. If you pray, you can offer it to God; if you don't, just loosen your grip on it for a moment.

wordCard.voice: Kunti. With the kingdom won, she walked into the forest, guiding Gandhari, and told her sons she had urged them on for their honor, not her own enjoyment. Today's word.

orig.note: Sanskrit, vanaprastha: the stage of life when one leaves the household for the forest (vana).

carryVoice: Your line: vanaprastha, a season for letting go. Kunti walked into it with Gandhari's hand on her shoulder. See you tomorrow.
